gap_or_question: Data 360 federation has no stated latency budget, and sub-second query performance for voice/chat is unproven at Vivo scale (Risk #4). Nine of the 15 FND stories (FND-02 + the 7 federation families FND-09..15 + FND-03) all rest on the same federated-query scaffold. If the latency target isn't achievable, the fallback is selective replication — a redesign that thickens FND and, because FND feeds S2 (the critical path), pressures the whole schedule. What is the required response-time SLA for a federated 360 read during a live voice/chat interaction, and has federation been proven at Vivo's customer-master scale?
impact_or_notes: Load-bearing on the majority of the epic. A replication redesign could push FND base (65-164 SP) materially higher and couple it to the S2 critical path. ROM flags 'validate early' but sets no target and carries no explicit contingency on FND. This is the single biggest estimate risk in the epic.

gap_or_question: FND is explicitly scoped as only the 'attendance slice' on top of the enterprise transversal Headless-360 platform (shared with B2X Commerce, Billing, ERP), which the ROM excludes as an out-of-scope program dependency (§2, §12, Risk #2). The ROM states 'if it delays, FND doesn't land and the agentic surface degrades' — yet gives no owner, no readiness date, and no confirmation the platform exists. Who is building the enterprise Headless-360 platform, on what timeline, and is it available before Sprint 0 of this engagement?
impact_or_notes: FND-01 (AI Trust Layer), FND-02 (Data-360 model) and FND-04 (runtime) assume a substrate that is neither in this ROM nor confirmed to exist. If the platform slips or must be partly built here, the FND estimate is understated and the entire program's Sprint-0 start is at risk. This is the epic's foundational assumption and it is unowned.

gap_or_question: FND-06 (Service Cloud Voice + Amazon Connect standup, 8-21 SP) assumes the AWS Connect instance is provisioned, CCaaS/AWS contracts are signed, and the Genesys telephony migration (EOL Dec/2027) has a path (Risk #8). None of that infrastructure provisioning is in the ROM. Are the AWS Connect instance and CCaaS contracts in place, who owns the telephony carrier/number migration, and what is the Genesys cutover plan?
impact_or_notes: FND-06 is the prerequisite for the entire OMNI voice subset. If the AWS/telephony foundation isn't contracted and provisioned, FND-06 blocks at Sprint 0 and cascades into S4. Infra provisioning outside the Salesforce build is not sized anywhere and needs an explicit owner and date.

gap_or_question: FND-01 (AI Trust Layer: grounding, masking, toxicity, audit) and FND-02 assume Agentforce grounding works over federated, minimal-resident Data 360 data rather than resident data — but the RAG/Data Library grounding path typically requires data in Data Cloud. Is Data Cloud/Data 360 licensed at the required tier, and is agent grounding a supported pattern over federated (non-resident) data at this scale? Separately, the per-family PII masking (FND-09..15) has no defined LGPD field-level masking ruleset — which fields are PII, and what are the masking/consent rules per family?
impact_or_notes: If grounding over federated data isn't a supported/proven pattern, the core agentic value proposition of FND-01 is at risk and may force resident data (compounding G0101). LGPD masking rules being undefined leaves FND-01 + the 7 federation families under-specified. [assumption: needs confirmation against Vivo's Data Cloud licensing and Agentforce grounding architecture]

gap_or_question: FND-05 (Passive-Core security & sharing model) is a single 5-13 SP Primary story, but must cover a tier-1 telco sharing model spanning federated data, field-level PII/LGPD masking, thousands of internal agents, and ~18k external Aliado partners on Experience Cloud (Risk #7). The ROM is also silent on the identity provider / SSO, MFA, and profile/permission-set strategy for agents and partners. What is the identity/SSO model, and does the sharing model include the partner-community licensing and external-surface sharing, or is that scoped elsewhere?
impact_or_notes: A passive-core sharing model with federated data, partner-community sharing, and PII masking is likely under-sized as one 5-13 SP story. Missing SSO/identity strategy is a foundational gap that every squad inherits. Partner-community licensing (18k Aliado) may belong here or in OMNI-28 — the boundary is unclear and risks a coverage gap.

gap_or_question: FND-03 (federated identity resolution across Salesforce + customer master + legacy) is a single derived 2-6 SP story, yet it must reconcile customer identity across multiple legacy systems (WDE, GPS, Next, Siebel) plus the master, likely with no shared key, at multi-million-customer scale. The matching/dedup logic, survivorship rules, and master-data governance are not described. What are the matching keys and confidence rules, and is there an existing golden-record/MDM source of truth to resolve against?
impact_or_notes: Cross-system identity resolution at telco scale is notoriously hard and is sized here as a small derived story. If matching logic and MDM governance must be built rather than consumed, FND-03 is materially under-sized and blocks CIM-04/05 (identify/verify) which sit on the critical path.

gap_or_question: FND is a shared foundation consumed by all five squads — the AI Trust Layer, Data-360 model, deterministic runtime (FND-04, reused by 6 CPM/COPM guided-flow families), and masking rules are cross-team assets. The ROM defines no configuration-ownership, data-stewardship, or change-management model for these shared components, nor how ownership is split with the enterprise Headless-360 platform team. Who governs the federated data model and masking rules as they evolve, and how are changes to the shared deterministic runtime coordinated across squads? (Buyer-facing governance question.)
impact_or_notes: Governance discipline probe: multi-team config ownership and data stewardship are triggered here because FND is a foundation every squad depends on. Without an ownership/change model, changes to FND-04 or the masking rules risk uncoordinated breakage across CPM/COPM/SDP. Not an auto-added epic — surface for the buyer to confirm whether a CoE / stewardship function is scoped.

gap_or_question: The ROM sizes OPS-01/05 as the mechanism to build the classification tree (palitagem) as hierarchical metadata plus a bulk import/export path, but is silent on the scale and provenance of the existing tree: how many contact-reason nodes exist in Vivo's current operation, whether that taxonomy is migrated 1:1 or rationalized, and who is the accountable data steward for it post-go-live. For a tier-1 telco the tree can run to hundreds or thousands of nodes across channels and product families. Question for Vivo: how large is the current palitagem, is it migrated as-is or curated, and who owns its ongoing governance (versioning, node retirement, eTOM alignment)?
impact_or_notes: OPS-01 (5-13 SP) prices the metadata engine, not the content load or the curation exercise. A large unmapped tree plus a manual eTOM-reconciliation effort (OPS-01 also claims eTOM mapping) is unbounded work that lands outside the sized band. No data-steward owner means the tree degrades after launch and the effort recurs. Highest-leverage OPS unknown.

gap_or_question: OPS-11 sizes the Entitlement Process + Milestones (SLA) engine per tier (5-13 SP), and the tiers are named (Gold/Silver/Platinum/Purpura/Prime/VivoV/VPR/Alto Valor). But the actual SLA targets — response/resolution times by tier x channel x case type — are not defined anywhere in the ROM, nor is it stated whether any are Anatel-mandated regulatory deadlines (Ouvidoria/reconsideracao timelines appear in CPM-09/10). Question for Vivo: who owns the SLA matrix, do current contractual/regulatory SLA definitions exist to load, and how many distinct entitlement combinations must be configured?
impact_or_notes: The engine is a few SP; the combinatorial matrix of tier x channel x case-type targets is the real work and is unscoped. Regulated response deadlines carry breach consequences (OPS-13 notifications) that raise the correctness bar. Missing SLA-ownership means no source of truth to configure against — a build blocker, not just a sizing risk.

gap_or_question: OPS-19 (message template library — approved WhatsApp templates, 3-8 SP) is priced as a Salesforce configuration item, but WhatsApp templates require Meta/BSP (Business Solution Provider) approval outside Salesforce, and the ROM is silent on the BSP/provider path (native Digital Engagement WhatsApp vs. a third-party BSP), the number of templates, and who owns submission/approval. Question for Vivo: which WhatsApp provider/BSP is in place, how many templates are in scope, and who manages the Meta approval lifecycle?
impact_or_notes: External approval dependency and lead time are not captured in the SP or the schedule. If a non-native BSP is used, an integration surface may be needed that isn't in INT scope. Template volume drives real config effort beyond the 3-8 SP envelope.

gap_or_question: OPS-20 sizes operational dashboards for AHT/ASA/abandonment (5-13 SP), but ASA (average speed of answer) and abandonment are contact-center/telephony metrics that originate in Amazon Connect / Service Cloud Voice, not in native Salesforce Case data. The ROM does not say how these metrics reach Salesforce for dashboarding — no Amazon Connect metrics ingestion, CCP/CTR pipeline, or Data 360 feed is called out in FND or INT for this purpose. Where does the AHT/ASA/abandonment data come from, and is the ingestion in scope?
impact_or_notes: If the metric source data must be ingested from Amazon Connect (analytics stream / contact records), that is an integration/data-engineering effort not present in the OPS SP nor the 36 INT Core clients. The dashboards are un-buildable on Salesforce-native data alone — this either inflates OPS or opens an unscoped INT/FND item.

gap_or_question: OPS-15/16/17/18 build the Knowledge authoring workflow, Data Category taxonomy, and governance (expiration/review), but the ROM is silent on migrating Vivo's existing knowledge content (article count, format, source system) and on who owns Knowledge governance and content design after launch (authoring authority, review cadence, quality). Question for Vivo: is there an existing knowledge base to migrate, how large is it, and who are the content owners/stewards going forward?
impact_or_notes: A net-new Knowledge workflow with no migration path and no named content authors is a stub — the mechanism ships empty. Article migration and content-design ownership are unscoped; SDP-11 (article recommendation) and CIM-09 (Knowledge in inquiry handling) degrade with no content behind them. Content-design/governance discipline signal.

gap_or_question: Premise 4 excludes OPS from the +12.5% functional-test adjustment on the basis that OPS is 'majoritariamente configuracao/plataforma.' Several OPS stories are genuinely coded behavior, not clicks: OPS-08 guided progressive cascade selector (LWC), OPS-10 post-case actions driven by disposition (automation/Apex), OPS-20/22 custom operational and agent-quality dashboards. Is the config-only classification accurate for the full OPS set, or do these coded items warrant test-adjusted effort?
impact_or_notes: If the coded OPS items carry real Apex/LWC, excluding the whole domain from functional-test DoD understates QA effort on the disposition-capture and dashboard surfaces — exactly the wrap-up path every agent touches on every case. A mis-classification here quietly understates the OPS band.

gap_or_question: CIM-17 'atualizacao de dados cadastrais' (5-13 SP) is a WRITE to the customer master, but the master is Vivo-owned and federated read-only via FND-11 (Party/Profile, TMF632). The Integration Roadmap (§4/§6) lists no transactional write client for party/profile updates — the re-anchored writes are only INT-08 (bill adjust), INT-11 (interaction), INT-22 (installment). Where does a cadastral change land, and through which client/facade?
impact_or_notes: CIM-17 is sized as if an update path exists; if a new Core/MULE write client to the master must be built, that effort sits outside the CIM band and outside the current INT count. Confirm the master-data write endpoint and its disposition (CORE vs MULE facade) before Phase 2, or CIM-17 and the INT floor are both understated.

gap_or_question: CIM-05 'verificar identidade/KYC com badge de autorizacao' carries the widest CIM band (8-21 SP) with no defined verification policy: which factors (knowledge-based, OTP, document, biometrics via INT-13 BiometryHistoryCallout), what step-up rules per channel (voice vs WhatsApp vs anonymous), and what regulatory basis (Anatel, LGPD) governs the authorization badge and what it unlocks downstream. Risk #6 notes the source identity flow had a wrong copy-pasted description.
impact_or_notes: KYC policy is the single largest driver of the CIM-05 band and cascades to CRM-12 (SIM swap re-verification) and every write-capable journey gated on the badge. Undefined factors/step-up = the 8->21 SP spread stays unresolved and the 50%-class uncertainty is effectively unquantified for this story.

gap_or_question: CIM-01 logs interaction as native EngagementInteraction, while INT-11 (CIMServiceCallout, TMF683, MULE Primary) writes interaction to the legacy system and FND-12 federates Party Interaction history read-only. Which store is the authoritative system of record for an interaction — Salesforce or legacy — and is CIM-01 a dual-write? If dual-write, who owns reconciliation and idempotency on failure (the ~22% non-2xx reality of Risk #3)?
impact_or_notes: An unspecified dual system-of-record for interactions is a build fork: single-write-to-Salesforce vs dual-write-with-reconciliation are materially different in effort and error handling. Affects CIM-01/02/03 sizing and the resilient error-handling assumption the INT 50% buffer rests on.

gap_or_question: CIM-12 'disparar pesquisa de satisfacao' and CIM-13 (non-response capture) assume a survey capability, but no survey platform is named — native Salesforce Feedback Management vs a third-party (Medallia/Qualtrics/other). No survey-platform integration client appears in the INT roadmap (INT-23/24 only send email/comms). How is the survey authored, delivered per channel, and scored/returned?
impact_or_notes: If a third-party survey platform is in play, a net-new integration client (not in the 36) is required and CIM-12's 3-5 SP is understated. If native Feedback Management, licensing and channel coverage (voice/WhatsApp) must be confirmed. Either way this is unsized today.

gap_or_question: Governance / data stewardship: consent and LGPD are scoped only at CRM-10 (consent + data-subject-request), but CIM-01 captures interactions across voice, WhatsApp, chat and transcription (OMNI-10/11) — recording and message retention that require consent capture and lawful-basis checks at the point of interaction. Who owns consent verification at capture time, call-recording notice/opt-out, and the retention/masking policy for interaction transcripts? Is there a data-stewardship owner for the federated identity/interaction data?
impact_or_notes: Buyer-facing question. Consent-at-capture is a regulatory exposure (LGPD, Anatel) not currently sized in CIM; if consent gating is required before logging/recording, it adds behavior to CIM-01 and the AI Trust Layer masking (FND-01). Absent a stewardship owner, this is a customer-readiness risk, not a build line.

gap_or_question: Experience design: CIM-06 (self-service eligibility + redirect) and CIM-08 (prospect/anonymous interaction) lack defined rules and journeys — what makes a request self-service-eligible, where deflection lands (app, IVR/OMNI-12, bot), and what an unverified/anonymous caller can do before the KYC gate (CIM-05) fires. Has deflection UX / self-service journey research been done, and by whom?
impact_or_notes: Buyer-facing question. Deflection eligibility and the anonymous-vs-verified boundary shape routing (CIM-07), self-service scope, and IVR handoff — left undefined they under-decompose CIM-06/08 (derived, 2-4 SP) and risk a deflection experience with no design basis. Flag whether experience/service design is in the delivery scope or a client dependency. [Grelha 2026-08-25 — Q4b RESOLVIDO EM ESCOPO (diretiva do scoper): coberto por track right-sized de service/conversation design no P&D, limitado às superfícies de alto impacto (console, fluxos do agente, motor de 300 passos). Ver ADR 0001.]

gap_or_question: The deterministic interview engine (CPM-04) — the load-bearing item of the whole domain, sized 13-21 SP and reused by 6 families — is DECLARED but NOT MODELED. No source flow decomposed the '300+ steps'; per Risks #1/#2 the Problem/Technical/Termination branches came from a pain corpus and platform research, not a modeled UPN flow. Where does the 300+ figure come from, and what is the actual step count, branching depth, and decision logic per family? Until the engine is modeled, 13-21 SP is a placeholder, not an estimate.
impact_or_notes: This is the single largest sizing bet in the epic and the reason CPM carries the 50% contingency. If real depth/regulatory branching materially exceeds the assumption, even +50% is insufficient — the whole S3 track (194-346 SP) re-baselines. Highest priority to model in Phase 0/1 before committing the range. [Grelha 2026-08-25: rebaixado de risco de re-baseline para item de de-risking da Fase 0 — modelar o fluxo para refinar os 13-21 SP do especialista, NÃO re-dimensionar.]

gap_or_question: The 'one engine, reused by 6 families' premise is unproven. CPM-20..24 (Fiber, TV, Convergent, VAS, Prepaid disputes) are each derived at a flat 4-6 SP as 30% intra-capacity derivations of CPM-04, and CPM-25 (guided dispatch) plus CPM-18/19 (migrations) also 'reuse the engine.' But the families diverge structurally: Prepaid has no monthly invoice (CPM-24 is a recharge/credit dispute, not a bill contest), Convergent must attribute a line item to the correct bundle leg, TV mixes IPTV/DTH. Does the engine genuinely generalize, or does each family carry its own regulatory dispute ruleset that breaks the flat-derivation math?
impact_or_notes: If per-family regulatory logic doesn't collapse into one reusable scaffold, the derived 4-6 SP per family understates each, and the reuse economics that justify the CPM sizing evaporate. Validate the engine's parameterization against 2-3 divergent families (Prepaid vs Convergent) early — Risk #2's 'regulatory variation per product' lives here. [RESOLVIDO na grelha 2026-08-25: reuso confirmado em primeira mão pelo scoper — dimensionado por arquiteto especialista que fez assessment presencial na Vivo. Manter CPM-20..24 em 4-6 SP; não alargar a banda.]

gap_or_question: CPM-04 has two hard cross-domain dependencies not reflected in S3's clean parallel schedule: it runs on the FND-04 deterministic orchestration runtime (S1) and writes the transactional adjustment via INT-08 (S5, a MuleSoft-facade bill-adjustment client, TMF678). The ROM assumes the Mule facade for INT-08 already exists (Risk #3a) and that FND-04 lands on time (Risk #2 — degrades if the shared Headless-360 platform slips). If either is late or the Mule facade must actually be built, CPM-04 and all six derivative families block, with no transactional write path.
impact_or_notes: S3 is scheduled as pure parallel construction (25-35 SP/sprint), but CPM-04 cannot complete-to-DoD ahead of FND-04 + INT-08. This is a sequencing dependency that the critical-path model doesn't surface. Confirm the FND-04 and INT-08 delivery order and whether the Mule bill-adjustment facade is in-scope for the integration program or a gap.

gap_or_question: Who owns change control and compliance for the regulated interview flows, both during build and after go-live? A 300+ step regulated dispute/migration flow changes whenever Anatel rules or STFC-concession terms change. The ROM sizes the build but is silent on the governance model: versioning/effective-dating of the engine flows (OPS-02 covers only the classification tree, not the interview engine), regulatory sign-off before a flow change ships, and a named accountable owner for Anatel compliance. Is there a client-side governance/CoE function, or is this an unscoped delivery obligation?
impact_or_notes: Governance discipline probe — buyer-facing. Regulated telco flows without a change-control owner become non-compliant the moment a rule shifts; this is a customer-readiness risk (weighted heaviest) that sits outside the build hours. Surface as a question; if the client owns it, note as dependency, if not, it's an activity to scope.

gap_or_question: There is no experience-design work scoped for the 300+ step guided flow, yet completion/abandonment of that flow directly drives the ARI success KPIs (-15% TMA, +FCR). How does an agent — and, in self-service, a customer — navigate a 300-step interview without fatigue, error, or drop-off? The ROM sizes the engine's construction (CPM-04) but no UX research, service design, or content design for progressive disclosure, resume/save, or agent guidance surfaces anywhere in CPM.
impact_or_notes: Experience-design discipline probe — buyer-facing. A technically-correct 300-step flow that agents can't run efficiently fails the exact TMA/FCR outcomes the investment is measured against. Ask whether experience/service design is expected; capture as an activity — either an owner is named or it goes to gaps as a risk to the success criteria. [Grelha 2026-08-25 — Q4b RESOLVIDO EM ESCOPO (diretiva do scoper): coberto por track right-sized de service/conversation design no P&D, limitado às superfícies de alto impacto (console, fluxos do agente, motor de 300 passos). Ver ADR 0001.]

gap_or_question: Anatel/Ouvidoria escalation (CPM-09 'Escalar para Ouvidoria/Anatel' and CPM-10 'Sincronizar status de reconsideracao Anatel') are each sized at 1 SP — the floor. But regulated-agency escalation carries statutory response windows, reconsideration-status synchronization with an external Anatel system, and legal exposure on missed deadlines. The ROM specifies neither the Anatel integration mechanism (is there a callout/EVENT client for status sync? none is listed in INT) nor the SLA/deadline model behind these flows.
impact_or_notes: 1 SP for a regulated-agency escalation with external status sync is almost certainly under-scoped, and no INT client backs CPM-10's 'sincronizar status.' If Anatel integration is real, this is both a missing integration story and an under-sized capability. Confirm the Anatel interface and deadline obligations.

gap_or_question: The mandatory regulated migrations — CPM-18 copper->fiber (end of STFC concession) and CPM-19 DTH->IPTV — are sized as single envelopes (4-6 / 1-2 SP) reusing the CPM-04 engine, but the ROM captures no regulatory deadline and defers campaign scale to 'capacity planning' (Risk #9: remaining copper base + ~300k DTH clients). A hard regulatory end-of-concession date would force sequencing and prioritization of CPM-18/19 ahead of other CPM work — a constraint the critical-path model doesn't reflect.
impact_or_notes: If the STFC-concession/DTH end dates fall inside the build window, these become deadline-driven must-ships, not backlog-ordered items, and the outbound/campaign volume (OMNI-27, CPM-08) may need dedicated capacity. Confirm the regulatory dates and whether they constrain the delivery sequence.

gap_or_question: Fraud handling (CPM-13, 8-21 SP) and legal/special-services legal-hold (CPM-15, 8-21 SP) carry the widest uncertainty bands in the domain and are declared, not modeled. Legal-hold implies data-retention, e-discovery, and access-restriction obligations; fraud implies a block/deprogramming + investigation workflow with its own escalation and audit. Neither the retention/hold data model, the investigation workflow ownership, nor the compliance constraints are specified.
impact_or_notes: The 8-21 SP bands signal the ROM knows these are unmodeled. Legal-hold in particular can impose org-wide data-retention and access controls that ripple beyond CPM. Model both in Phase 1 and confirm the compliance obligations before locking the range.

gap_or_question: The V360 cockpit (CRM-01..07) reads its profile/segment/NPS, financial, product-inventory, open-order and interaction-timeline panels from the seven federated Data 360 families (FND-09..15). ROM Risk #4 flags that sub-second federated-query latency at Vivo scale is unproven, but that risk is booked against the FND track — the CRM outcome silently inherits it. Is sub-second panel render over federated data a validated design point, or a bet to prove in Phase 0/early spike?
impact_or_notes: The cockpit is the ARI headline outcome and the -15% TMA success criterion rides on it. If federation can't hit sub-second latency, the fallback (selective replication) thickens FND and couples to the S2 critical path — the exact schedule bottleneck the ROM warns about. A slow single pane fails the 'eliminate Alt+Tab' promise as badly as no pane. Validate latency early against real Vivo volumes before committing the render architecture.

gap_or_question: Production telemetry shows ~22% non-2xx callout responses and 19 source services slated to RETIRE. The seven cockpit panels each depend on a federated family that can be slow, erroring, or partially unavailable. The ROM specifies no partial-data, stale-data, or source-down behavior for the unified 360 view — what does the cockpit render when a family (e.g. Customer Bill or Trouble Ticket history) fails or is stale?
impact_or_notes: A single-pane cockpit is only trusted if the agent knows when a panel is complete, stale, or blank-because-broken. Silent gaps in the 360 view during a live call actively mislead the agent and erode FCR. Graceful degradation, freshness indicators, and per-panel error states are unscoped behavior that materially affects CRM-01..07 sizing and the credibility of the whole surface.

gap_or_question: Contextual next-best-action (CRM-08) and explainable churn signal via SHAP (CRM-13) both presuppose a scoring/recommendation model. INT-19 (RtdNbaNboServiceCallout, TMF680) implies an external NBA/NBO engine, but the source and ownership of the churn model and its SHAP explanations are unstated. Is the churn/NBA model Vivo-provided (we consume scores + explanations), or must this engagement build, train, and explain it?
impact_or_notes: CRM-08 (5-8 SP) and CRM-13 (1-2 SP) are sized as thin consumption/surfacing stories. If model authoring, feature engineering, or MLOps/monitoring fall inside scope, the domain is materially under-scoped and pulls in a data-science capability the ROM doesn't roster. If Vivo owns the model, the SHAP-explanation contract (payload, feature naming) becomes a load-bearing integration dependency to confirm.

gap_or_question: LGPD consent capture and data-subject-request handling (CRM-10) is sized 5-8 SP as a Salesforce-resident capability, but Vivo owns the customer master and most 360 data is federated, not resident. A data-subject-request (erasure, portability, access) must execute across the federated estate Vivo owns, not just the minimal-resident Salesforce records. Who is accountable for consent stewardship and end-to-end DSR fulfillment across federated systems, and is that workstream in scope?
impact_or_notes: Governance discipline probe (buyer-facing). A DSR that only clears Salesforce-resident data while master/legacy copies persist is a compliance false-positive under LGPD. There is no data-stewardship or governance workstream in the ROM. Confirm whether CRM-10 is consent/DSR intake-and-orchestration only (with fulfillment delegated) or full cross-estate fulfillment — the two are wildly different in effort and accountability.

gap_or_question: The unified agentic cockpit is THE headline UX outcome of the ARI (success criterion #1: single front-end eliminating Alt+Tab across WDE/GPS/Next/Siebel; -15% TMA). The ROM sizes the build of CRM-01..13 but no experience-design activity — agent research/observation, service design, information hierarchy of the seven panels, content design, usability validation with real agents. Who designs and validates the cockpit UX before build, and is that effort owned by this engagement or the client?
impact_or_notes: Experience-design discipline probe (buyer-facing). A cockpit built to a guessed panel layout risks recreating fragmentation in one window and missing the TMA target that justifies the whole ARI. Design is an implied activity, not a line in the ROM — surface it so the buyer decides whether it's scoped here, owned by Vivo, or a gap. Weight this heavily: it is the outcome the investment is measured on. [Grelha 2026-08-25 — Q4b RESOLVIDO EM ESCOPO (diretiva do scoper): coberto por track right-sized de service/conversation design no P&D, limitado às superfícies de alto impacto (console, fluxos do agente, motor de 300 passos). Ver ADR 0001.]

gap_or_question: Ownership change with document validation (CRM-11, 5-8 SP) spans three domains: document validation via INT-12 (DocumentRepository) and INT-13 (Biometry), and the actual asset title transfer coordinated with PROCP-15 (change-ownership capture). CRM-11 is sized as if self-contained — where is the boundary between the CRM consent/validation capture and the PROCP transactional ownership transfer, and are the INT-12/13 clients assumed available?
impact_or_notes: Cross-domain dependency risks either double-counting (transfer sized in both CRM-11 and PROCP-15) or a gap (each assumes the other owns the transactional write). Confirm the seam: CRM-11 as the identity/document-validation front-half handing off to PROCP-15 for the asset move. Also confirm INT-12/INT-13 (both CORE Primary) land before or with CRM-11, or CRM-11 stalls.

gap_or_question: The ARI success criteria (-15% TMA, improved FCR) are the measurable outcomes the V360 cockpit must move, but no current TMA or FCR baseline — per channel, journey, or segment — is stated in the ROM or nomination. What are today's baselines, how are they instrumented, and who owns measuring the delta post-go-live?
impact_or_notes: Without a documented baseline the headline outcome can't be evidenced, and the renewal-insurance value case (proving ROI to a Neutral decision-maker/COO) has nothing to measure against. This is a program-level gap that lands hardest on V360 as the surface the KPIs attach to. Baseline capture is a discovery/instrumentation task to scope, not invent. [Grelha 2026-08-25 — Q4a RESOLVIDO EM ESCOPO (diretiva do scoper): captura+congelamento do baseline TMA/FCR e plano de medição (reconciliar Connect+Omni) entram no P&D como atividade definida. Ver ADR 0001.]

gap_or_question: The Pillar 2 MCP handoff contract that all of PROCP depends on is undefined in the ROM. There is no agreed schema for the submit payload (COPM-02), the catalog/pricing MCP tool signatures PROCP consumes, or the acknowledgement/reconciliation semantics. ROM Risk #5 names this as the biggest dependency but the contract itself does not exist yet. What is the actual submit payload, tool interface, and response contract Pillar 2 will expose? (Inventing this schema is out of bounds — it must be confirmed against Pillar 2, not assumed.)
impact_or_notes: Single largest risk to E06. If the contract is not stable, COPM-02 submission and handoff reconciliation block and captured orders have nowhere to go — the entire capture engine stalls. Drives the 50% PROCP contingency. Must be pinned in a joint Pillar 2/Pillar 3 design session before Phase 2 story detailing.

gap_or_question: Governance probe: who owns and versions the cross-pillar MCP contract? The ROM treats catalog, pricing and order-management as consumed/delegated but names no owner for the contract itself, no versioning or backward-compatibility policy, no breaking-change process, and no availability/latency SLA between the capture layer (ours) and Pillar 2. When Pillar 2 changes a tool signature or catalog shape, what protects the capture flows from breaking?
impact_or_notes: Buyer-facing governance question. Cross-pillar contracts fail silently without a named owner and a change-control process. Absent this, every Pillar 2 change is an unplanned rework event on PROCP/COPM. Needs a contract-ownership and versioning agreement at program level, not inside the epic.

gap_or_question: COPM-02 submits the captured order to Pillar 2 and 'reconciles the handoff', but the failure and exception semantics are undefined: what happens when the submission is rejected, times out, or partially succeeds? Is submission idempotent, is there retry, are there compensating actions to release reserved resources (SIM/MSISDN/CPE/decoder/slot) on a failed handoff, and what state does the customer/agent see? ROM is silent.
impact_or_notes: Capture reserves scarce resources before submission; a failed or ambiguous handoff without compensation leaks reservations and leaves orders in limbo. This is core transactional-integrity behavior the build must author but has no spec for — high rework risk if assumed wrong.

gap_or_question: PROCP-01, the agentic capture engine, is explicitly a new, unproven capability at Vivo tier-1 scale. The ROM does not define the autonomy boundary: where the agent acts autonomously vs. requires human-in-the-loop, the guardrails on eligibility/config decisions, or acceptance criteria for 'captured correctly'. What are the confidence/authority limits and the fallback to agent-assisted capture?
impact_or_notes: The agentic capture engine anchors all 19 PROCP stories via reuse. If autonomy limits and guardrails are undefined, both build effort and regulatory/mis-order exposure are unbounded. Drives the 50% PROCP buffer alongside the contract risk. Prove the engine early on Mobile activation before deriving the family variants.

gap_or_question: The ROM calls the family x operation decomposition an 'honest matrix — not every operation applies to every family' but does not pin which combinations are in scope vs. deliberately excluded. The 19 stories cover a subset (e.g. move/change-ownership/device-upgrade appear for some families, not others). Which family x operation cells are committed for delivery, which are deferred, and on what basis?
impact_or_notes: Without an explicit in/out matrix, scope creep is inevitable during Phase 2 as un-enumerated cells surface as 'assumed in scope'. Each derived cell is real build effort. Needs a confirmed coverage matrix to hold the 66-112 SP base honest.

gap_or_question: The boundary between what PROCP sources from Core integration clients (INT), from Data 360 federation, and from Pillar 2 MCP tools is not resolved for the capture steps. Serviceability, for example, appears both as a Core client (INT-04 ServiceCoverageAvailabilityCallout) and as an MCP-consumed concern; resource reservation (SIM/MSISDN, CPE, decoder, install slot) has no named owner of the reservation ledger. Which capture steps are Core-direct, which are MCP, and who owns the reservation system of record?
impact_or_notes: If serviceability/eligibility/reservation are double-sourced or mis-routed, capture logic is built against the wrong system and reservations can conflict with Pillar 2's own inventory truth. Interacts with the Integration Routing Rule (premise 17) and Risk #3. Must be dispositioned per step before build.

gap_or_question: Experience design probe: the agentic capture flow UX is not designed. How does the conversational/guided capture behave across families and operations — turn-by-turn eligibility->serviceability->config, error recovery when a resource is unavailable, agent-assisted vs. autonomous framing, and the handoff moment to the customer/agent? No service-design or content-design work is scoped for the capture surface.
impact_or_notes: Buyer-facing experience-design question. A tier-1 agentic capture flow spanning seven families is a substantial UX/content design effort that the ROM's engineering-only estimate does not carry. If the client team does not own it, it is an unscoped activity that affects adoption and the -15% AHT success criterion. [Grelha 2026-08-25 — Q4b RESOLVIDO EM ESCOPO (diretiva do scoper): coberto por track right-sized de service/conversation design no P&D, limitado às superfícies de alto impacto (console, fluxos do agente, motor de 300 passos). Ver ADR 0001.]

gap_or_question: ROM Risk #6 flags that the source flows feeding PROCP are low quality: all in draft state, reserve-resources with empty Notes, add/remove-VAS with a duplicated billing activity, activity numbering not mapped to node IDs. These are the exact reusable processes (serviceability, reserve-resources, configure-products) the capture engine decomposes from. Have these source flows been reconciled, or does PROCP decomposition rest on unreliable inputs?
impact_or_notes: PROCP story magnitudes derive from source flows that are explicitly unreliable. Un-reconciled, the per-family/per-operation SP could shift materially. ROM directs reconciliation before individual PROCP/COPM story detailing in Phase 2 — this is a prerequisite, not a refinement.

gap_or_question: COPM-02 is the epic's crux — 'submit captured order (from PROCP) to Pillar 2 management via MCP and reconcile the handoff' — yet the reconciliation contract is undefined. What does 'reconcile' concretely mean: is the MCP submission synchronous with an immediate accept/reject, or async (fire-and-forget with a later status callback)? What state model does Pillar 2 return (order-accepted / in-fulfillment / partial / failed), what correlation/idempotency key ties a Salesforce request to a Pillar 2 order so a retry doesn't double-submit, and what is the compensation/rollback path when Pillar 2 rejects after PROCP has already reserved a resource? Inventing the Pillar 2 payload/state schema is out of bounds — flag to confirm against Pillar 2's actual MCP resource contract.
impact_or_notes: This is Risk #5 (product-order boundary contract) landing directly on the epic. Premise #19 delegates management to Pillar 2 but the ROM explicitly notes the handoff contract is 'de posse fora deste escopo.' If the MCP contract isn't stable, COPM-02 and the reconciliation block outright and captured orders have nowhere to land — the 8-13 SP on COPM-02 assumes a contract that doesn't yet exist. Highest-priority dependency; drives a workshop and a Phase-0 reconciliation of Pillar 2's exposed resources before COPM-02 can be detailed.

gap_or_question: COPM-03 tracks order status and updates the customer (given a 2 SP floor for polling + UI update), but the ROM is silent on how status arrives from Pillar 2. Does Pillar 2 push status events (webhook / platform-event / MCP notification) that Salesforce subscribes to, or must Salesforce poll an MCP resource on a cadence? If polling, at what interval and what is the expected order volume — because polling at B2C scale has very different sizing and platform-limit implications than event subscription.
impact_or_notes: The choice (push vs poll) is load-bearing for both the COPM-03 design and the 'notify completion + close' (COPM-04) trigger — a poll model with no completion event forces a heuristic close. Directly coupled to G0701's async question. ROM silence here is the gap.

gap_or_question: COPM-05 (number portability) reuses the CPM-04 interview engine natively but then hands off to a 'clearinghouse.' Which clearinghouse/broker (in BR this is the centralizing portability entity governed by Anatel)? What is the handoff protocol, and — critically — the regulated portability SLA windows (request, validation, scheduled port, reversal window) the flow must enforce? How are clearinghouse rejections, donor-carrier disputes, and port reversals surfaced back into the guided journey? Inventing the clearinghouse integration schema is out of bounds — flag to confirm against Vivo's actual portability broker interface.
impact_or_notes: Portability is a hard-regulated, time-boxed process; the 8-13 SP on COPM-05 covers the native interview engine but the clearinghouse integration (a distinct external system, separate from the Pillar 2 MCP boundary) is unspecified. If the broker interface isn't MCP-invocable or is batch/file-based, the 'native guided flow' assumption weakens and the story may need an integration spike.

gap_or_question: COPM-06 (guided debt negotiation) does installment simulation and 'writes the agreement' via INT-22 (TMF651 PaymentAgreementCallout, Mule). The agreement write is delegated, but where do the installment simulation rules live — interest/discount schedules, minimum installment values, down-payment rules, eligibility (tenure, debt age, prior-default) policy? Are these authored in the Salesforce interview engine, consumed from Pillar 2/billing as a tool, or hard-coded? Who is the source of truth for the negotiation policy?
impact_or_notes: If the simulation policy must be built into the interview engine, COPM-06's 2-4 SP (a Derived story) is likely under-scoped; if consumed from an external pricing/collections engine, that's an unnamed integration dependency. Also compliance-sensitive under BR over-indebtedness law (Lei 14.181/Superendividamento) — see G0706.

gap_or_question: COPM-07 (reverse logistics of leased/comodato equipment on termination) captures the return, computes pro-rata, and tracks — triggered by the PROCP-17 disconnect. But no reverse-logistics/collection provider integration is named. How is physical pickup or drop-off scheduled and confirmed (Correios, a logistics partner, retail-store return), and how does return confirmation (or non-return, triggering a penalty charge) flow back to close the envelope and to billing? What master holds the leased-asset inventory that identifies what must be returned?
impact_or_notes: COPM-07 is scoped 1-3 SP as a thin envelope, but 'captures return, pro-rata, tracks' implies a fulfillment/logistics integration and a non-return penalty path that aren't in the ROM. Depends on the PROCP-17 disconnect trigger and on the same leased-asset source COPM-01 uses to identify the active asset. ROM silence is the gap; confirm whether the logistics handoff is in-scope or a delivery dependency like Product Design (Risk #11).

gap_or_question: Governance / discipline probe (buyer-facing): the three guided regulated journeys in this epic — number portability (Anatel portability rules), debt negotiation (BR over-indebtedness law), and reverse logistics of leased equipment (consumer/comodato obligations) — each carry regulatory and audit exposure. Who owns regulatory compliance sign-off, the approval of interview-script content and decision logic, and the audit-trail/evidence requirements for each journey? Is there a Vivo compliance/legal owner and a change-control process for updating the guided scripts when regulation changes?
impact_or_notes: The interview engine (CPM-04) mechanically renders whatever policy it's given; correctness against regulation is a business-ownership question the ROM doesn't assign. Without a named compliance owner and a script change-control process, the regulated journeys carry hidden rework and go-live risk. Surface as a buyer-facing question — do not auto-add a compliance-governance epic.

gap_or_question: No policy envelope is defined for the Active Retention Agent's autonomous billing-friction resolution (SDP-13). What adjustments/credits may the agent grant without a human? What value thresholds, product families, or customer tiers bound autonomous action, and which decisions always escalate to a person?
impact_or_notes: This is the crux the ROM itself flags (Risk #10b, SDP override note): SDP-13 is the least-proven item — autonomous decision + policy-bound execution. The policy is the load-bearing spec; without it SDP-13 is unbuildable and unsafe. Blocks the largest, riskiest piece of the epic (SDP-13/14/15 = ~21-34 SP of 66-106).

gap_or_question: Where is the line between 'suggests' and 'executes'? SDP-05 is an active copilot that suggests AND executes; SDP-13 acts autonomously. Which specific actions from the SDP-01 catalog fire without agent confirmation or customer consent, and which are propose-only?
impact_or_notes: Defines the authorization scope enforced by the AI Trust Layer (FND-01 dependency). A wide 'execute' surface is materially harder to build and govern than an editable-recommendation surface (SDP-08). Unresolved, it swings both effort and risk for SDP-05/13; the two Primary-classified agentic patterns hang on this line.

gap_or_question: The epic carries the ARI success criteria (-15% TMA, +FCR, single agentic front-end), but no current TMA/FCR baseline is captured and no measurement instrumentation is designed beyond a single analytics story (CIM-19). How is baseline established, and how are TMA/FCR attributed to the agentic layer?
impact_or_notes: Without a sourced baseline the target cannot be validated or claimed at go-live. Do not invent a baseline — this needs Vivo's current operational metrics. CIM-19 (conversational analytics for TMA/FCR) is a single derived 1-SP story and looks under-scoped for measuring the epic's headline outcomes. [Grelha 2026-08-25 — Q4a RESOLVIDO EM ESCOPO (diretiva do scoper): captura+congelamento do baseline TMA/FCR e plano de medição (reconciliar Connect+Omni) entram no P&D como atividade definida. Ver ADR 0001.]

gap_or_question: SDP-01 (catalog of invocable actions) and SDP-02 (plan assembly) have value only once the underlying actions exist — INT Core clients, PROCP capture, CPM guided flows, OPS Knowledge/disposition. SDP sits in S4 but its agentic surface is functionally downstream of S2/S3/S5 outputs. How is this cross-domain sequencing dependency managed?
impact_or_notes: The ROM schedules SDP inside S4 but S2 is the critical path; the agentic front-end has little to invoke until S2/S3/S5 land. This coupling is not reflected in the parallel-squad model — risk that SDP integration slips to the tail regardless of S4's own velocity. [assumption: inferred from action-catalog dependency, not stated as a schedule link]

gap_or_question: SDP carries a 35% contingency buffer while hosting the single least-proven item in the whole ROM (the Active Retention Agent — autonomous decision + policy-bound execution). CPM, PROCP and INT get 50% for lower-novelty reasons. Is 35% defensible for SDP given SDP-13/14/15 were force-promoted to Primary precisely because autonomy is materially harder?
impact_or_notes: Internal estimation coherence gap. The architect override acknowledges chain-derivation would collapse these to 1-2 SP and understate risk — yet the buffer treats the domain as standard-uncertainty. If autonomy proves as hard as the note implies, SDP's max may exceed the 100-161 SP range.

gap_or_question: SDP-14/15 detect purchase intent and hand off to human sales, but sales/acquisition journeys (r2a-sales-journey-b2c) are explicitly out of scope. Where does the intelligent handoff land — what sales queue, lead/opportunity capture, or routing — and who owns building the receiving end?
impact_or_notes: The handoff has no defined target inside this scope. Either the receiving sales process is a delivery dependency on the adjacent sales/product-order domain, or SDP-15's value is stranded. Needs a boundary decision before SDP-14/15 are refined in Phase 2.

gap_or_question: Governance probe: what governs the autonomous agent's model grounding, PII masking, decision auditability and Anatel/LGPD compliance for autonomous billing resolution and intent detection? Does Vivo have an AI-governance / Center-of-Excellence function to own agent policy, drift monitoring, and the human-review/audit trail?
impact_or_notes: FND-01 (AI Trust Layer — grounding, masking, toxicity, audit) is the technical substrate, but the ROM defines no governance operating model for autonomous decisions in a regulated telecom under LGPD (CRM-10 consent). Autonomous action on customer billing without an audit/appeal path is a regulatory and trust exposure. Buyer-facing readiness question — flag, do not scope a role.

gap_or_question: Experience-design probe: replacing the legacy Alt+Tab/iframe operation with a single agentic conversational surface (SDP-03, CRM-01) for a large agent population (~18k+ including the Aliado channel) is a major experience and behavior shift. Is there a service-design / agent-experience-research and change-adoption workstream for the new front-end?
impact_or_notes: Adoption hinges on agents trusting AI suggestions and disposition/response automation (SDP-08/10/12); no experience-design or change-management activity is scoped. Ties to Risk #7 (Aliado channel under-decomposed). Surface as an activity for the expert to own or route to a delivery dependency — the single agentic front-end is an ARI success criterion, so adoption failure defeats the epic's purpose. Ver ADR 0001.]

Is satisfaction survey delivered by reusing the comms-send client, or does it require a dedicated survey-platform client (e.g. Qualtrics/Medallia) that is not in the 36? gap_or_question: The 17 MULE dispositions (plus INT-29) assume the MuleSoft facades already exist and only the thin Core client is in scope (premise 17, Risk #3a, Exclusion table). gap_or_question: Who owns the API contract for the Mule facade seam, and how are versioning and breaking changes governed? The Core clients (17 MULE) are consumers of an externally-owned facade contract, yet no owner, versioning scheme, deprecation policy, or change-notification process is defined for the Salesforce-team <-> MuleSoft-team boundary.
impact_or_notes: Buyer-facing governance probe. Determines whether the 50% contingency covers integration churn or is consumed by it. [Grelha 2026-08-25 — Q3 resolvida via opção 2: scoper NÃO tem o inventário de fachadas MuleSoft em mãos. gap_or_question: The ~22% non-2xx rate mixes systemic failure with legitimate business responses (expected 400/404 in eligibility/lookup), and the ROM states the proportion is not separable from the callout log alone (premise 9, Risk #3). Resilient error handling (retry, circuit-breaker, surface-to-agent vs auto-recover) cannot be designed per-endpoint without a per-family/per-status error taxonomy. Where does the transient-vs-terminal classification come from?
impact_or_notes: The resilient error-handling that current state lacks is the epic's core value, and it can't be built correctly against an unclassified error signal — wrong retry policy either hammers a failing dependency or gives up on a recoverable call. Needs an error-taxonomy discovery pass in Phase 1/2.

gap_or_question: The ROM does not address Salesforce platform callout governor limits against production volume (~2.3M callouts/business-day, peak ~2.9M, per premise 9). Have per-transaction and 24-hour callout limits, async/queued patterns, and bulkification been validated for the rebuilt Core clients at this scale? [assumption: callout-limit architecture not covered in ROM]
impact_or_notes: At 2.3M+ synchronous callouts/day, naive per-record Apex callouts can hit org limits and force an async/Platform-Event redesign — a structural change that would inflate INT effort beyond the 50% buffer. A Salesforce-native architecture concern that belongs in early integration design validation.

gap_or_question: INT is excluded from the +12.5% test adjustment because it carries its own contract-test strategy (premise 4), but that strategy — its owner, tooling, and the source-of-truth API specs (WSDL/OpenAPI/TMF schemas) each client maps its DTO against — is asserted, not defined. Where are the authoritative contracts for the 36 clients, and who authors and maintains the contract tests?
impact_or_notes: DTO mapping and contract tests can't be built without authoritative specs; the 74 WebService__c services normalized to TMF families are the starting point, but a normalized-to-family mapping is not a per-endpoint contract. If specs are stale or missing, mapping becomes reverse-engineering — a hidden effort driver on the highest-uncertainty axis.

gap_or_question: OMNI-28 (Aliado/Partner service surface, Experience Cloud, ~18k users) is represented by a SINGLE story sized 13-21 SP at the top of the band. A dominant external persona at that population scale almost certainly hides substantial undecomposed work: licensing model (Partner/Customer Community vs Community Plus vs External Apps), sharing/visibility model for the external channel, dedicated routing for the Aliado segment (own queues/skills/priority), mass onboarding/provisioning of the ~18k partners, functional parity of the service surface vs internal agent, and the partner journey/experience. This is ROM Risk #7. A dedicated decomposition pass is required if the Aliado channel is in delivery scope. Buyer question: is the Aliado channel in scope for this delivery phase, and what licensing/sharing model is intended?
impact_or_notes: Material under-estimation of the solution's largest user group. If resolved only in Phase 2 without re-sizing, OMNI can expand significantly (licensing, sharing, and surface parity are multi-story each). Risk of a commercial commitment made on a line that has not yet been decomposed.

gap_or_question: Who owns the SCV + Amazon Connect telephony infrastructure? ROM Risk #8 marks SCV + Amazon Connect provisioning, telephony migration (Genesys EOL Dec-2027), and AWS CCaaS contracts as infra prerequisites OUTSIDE the Salesforce build — yet the entire OMNI voice subset depends on them (OMNI-03/04/05/06/07/10). Questions: (a) do the Amazon Connect tenant and AWS account already exist or will they be provisioned in time? (b) is the Genesys->Connect migration this team's responsibility or a third party's? (c) is an AWS CCaaS contract signed? [assumption: without an AWS/Connect contract and provisioned tenant, ~40% of OMNI stories (the whole voice subset) are blocked regardless of Salesforce effort].
impact_or_notes: External dependency on the voice-domain critical path. An infra block invalidates the S4 schedule. Genesys EOL Dec-2027 imposes a hard window. Without ownership clarity, handoff/schedule risk lands on the Salesforce delivery with no lever to mitigate it.

gap_or_question: What is the source of truth for the operational metrics AHT/ASA/abandonment? Operational dashboards (OPS-20) declare AHT/ASA/abandonment, but real routing and queueing live partly in Amazon Connect (OMNI-03 queues mapped to Connect, OMNI-04 presence mapped to Connect). Questions: do these metrics come from Amazon Connect (CTRs/streams), from Salesforce Omni-Channel, or from reconciling both? Is there double-counting/divergence when a call traverses IVR->Connect->Omni? [assumption: if the IVR/queue is Connect and human routing is Omni, AHT/ASA/abandonment measured only in Salesforce omit pre-routing time and won't reconcile with contact-center reports].
impact_or_notes: Without defining the metric source and capture point, service KPIs (baseline and SLA) are neither auditable nor comparable to the legacy. Affects OPS-20 acceptance and any contractual SLA target. Do not invent a baseline — the source is required before sizing reporting. Pairs with G0507/G0903 (baseline gaps). [Grelha 2026-08-25 — Q4a RESOLVIDO EM ESCOPO (diretiva do scoper): captura+congelamento do baseline TMA/FCR e plano de medição (reconciliar Connect+Omni) entram no P&D como atividade definida. Ver ADR 0001.]

gap_or_question: Where is consent and recording at the point of capture for voice and digital channels under LGPD/Anatel? CRM-10 covers LGPD consent + DSR at the relationship level, and OMNI-10/11 cover call transcription, but no OMNI story addresses: (a) recording notice/consent at call start (voice), (b) opt-in/opt-out for WhatsApp/chat messaging (OMNI-17/21), (c) retention/purge of transcripts and media (OMNI-11 persists transcript — for how long? on what legal basis?), (d) Anatel recording/retention requirements for regulated service. Buyer question: what are the consent-at-capture and retention rules for voice and digital?
impact_or_notes: Tier-1 telco in a regulated process (Anatel + LGPD). Recording/transcription without consent and a retention policy is direct legal exposure. Likely un-sized work: IVR banner/notice, per-channel opt-in management, media/transcript retention policy, DSR fulfillment over recordings. Pairs with G0305 (CIM consent-at-capture).

gap_or_question: Who owns WhatsApp/Meta BSP onboarding and template governance? OMNI-17 (Digital Engagement WhatsApp/chat/email), OMNI-21 (attachments), and OMNI-27 (proactive outbound) depend on a BSP-approved WhatsApp Business number and Meta-approved message templates (HSM), subject to categories, the 24h window, and opt-in. No OMNI story covers: BSP approval/registration, the Meta template-approval cycle, opt-in management, and ongoing template-governance process. [assumption: if Vivo already runs WhatsApp via another BSP, there is un-captured number migration/re-registration and template re-approval work].
impact_or_notes: Meta/BSP approval is an external dependency with its own lead time (days to weeks) and evolving rules. Proactive outbound (OMNI-27) and the mandatory campaign migration (Risk #9) are unviable without approved templates. Template governance is an ongoing operation, not a one-off — needs a named owner.

gap_or_question: Who governs routing rules, queues, skills, and priority after go-live? OMNI-01/02/03 build priority/capacity/skill routing and queues mapped to Connect, but there is no operational ownership definition: who creates/changes queues and skill rules, who approves priority changes, how routing changes are versioned and tested, and where governance lives when routing is split between Omni (Salesforce) and Connect (AWS). Buyer-facing governance-discipline question: is there a contact-center configuration CoE/owner, or is this left to ad-hoc admins?
impact_or_notes: Omnichannel routing is live configuration with high operational change frequency. Without a governance model (who, approval, test, Omni/Connect split), the buyer inherits operational risk and configuration drift.
